name: Red Sea, Yemen and Saudi Arabia
label: CRITICAL

All three are party claims. The level holds at 5 and the trend stays escalating. Reassessed 24 November. Since 22 November: the coalition said it intercepted three Houthi ballistic missiles fired at Riyadh on 21 November and destroyed another drone aimed at the south, with no casualties reported (party claim, I-1197). Since 22 November: the Houthi-run health ministry said Saudi aircraft struck a state oil company fuel station in Sanaa and injured six employees, and the coalition said it destroyed a Houthi drone launched toward Riyadh with no casualties or damage reported (party claims, I-1190). A Houthi claim of a direct hit on the Rabigh refinery appeared in search results, but no fetched page carries it and it is not used. The level holds at 5 and the trend stays escalating. Reassessed 22 November. Reports of further Saudi strikes on Hodeidah on 21 and 22 November appeared in search results that no fetched page confirms and are not used. The level holds at 5 and the trend stays escalating. Coalition reports of further Houthi missiles at Riyadh that searches returned were not dated by a fetched page with certainty and are not used. The level holds at 5 and the trend stays escalating. Reassessed 20 November. Since 19 November: Saudi authorities said the Public Investment Fund Tower in Riyadh's financial centre was hit and several floors damaged with no injuries, and the coalition's initial assessment was falling debris (party claim, I-1159); the coalition reported five drones and one ballistic missile intercepted on 20 November (party claim, I-1160); the Associated Press reported that Saudi Arabia launched a major air campaign across Houthi-held Yemen earlier this week (I-1161). The AP report of a Saudi air campaign adds to the Saudi strikes already recorded (I-1043); the level holds at 5 and the trend stays escalating.
sponsor_posture: Houthis act with Iranian backing; Saudi Arabia and its coalition retaliate in Yemen.
cyber_nexus: Pro-Iran hacktivist personas target Gulf financial and government sites; Unit 42 reports Saudi ERP credential phishing and utility-bill scams. Egypt's authorisation of defensive support could add Egyptian banks and government portals to these personas' target set.
scenario: A Houthi strike closes Riyadh's airport for days during a regional leadership meeting, stranding staff, while phishing lures impersonate Saudi utility and payment portals.
so_what: Travel and staff safety in Saudi Arabia, Red Sea and Suez shipping insurance, and a second chokepoint on Gulf energy exports.
outlook: Next 72 hours: further Houthi salvos on Riyadh, the Eastern Province, the southern provinces and the East-West Pipeline corridor are very likely, with coalition strikes on Sanaa and the Red Sea coast continuing. Next 30 days: sustained pressure on Saudi airports and western export infrastructure is likely; an Egyptian deployment would likely stay defensive and limited, and Houthi action against Red Sea and Suez traffic in response to Egypt's move remains unlikely. The Tehran channel and the reported Saudi offer give a narrow route to restraint; carrier suspensions will likely run through November.

name: Strait of Hormuz and the Gulf
label: CRITICAL
key_judgment: Iran will very likely keep the strait effectively closed to unescorted traffic: UKMTO logged up to two more tanker hits near Khasab on 21 November after one on 20 November, and Trump told Axios he is not rushing into any decision on Iran, so the timing of a US strike package stays open and the Qatari reopening sequence remains the main path to a reopening.
basis: Reassessed 26 November. Since 24 November: UKMTO reported an outbound tanker struck by an unknown projectile about 18 nautical miles east of Khasab on 25 November, all crew accounted for (I-1207), and Al Jazeera, citing Marine Traffic, put crossings at 125 vessels from 17 to 23 November against 226 from 1 to 7 November (I-1208). An IRGC claim of two further mine strikes on 26 November appears only on a live blog and is not used. The level holds at 5 and the trend stays escalating. Reassessed 25 November. Since 24 November: the Maritime Executive, relaying UKMTO's industry sources, reported three tankers hit within about 17 minutes on the night of 22 November, with all crew accounted for and the vessels still under way; UKMTO has not named a cause (I-1203). The IRGC's mine claim of 24 November (I-1193) stays a party claim. No reopening bargain or US strike decision has been reported. The level holds at 5 and the trend stays escalating. Reassessed 24 November. Since 23 November: the WSJ, relayed by Reuters, reported a US investigation of up to 50 tanker cyberattacks with Iran a primary suspect and Russia possible, and an administration official said no evidence yet links Iran (I-1195, I-1196); the Treasury sanctioned more than two dozen Iranian exchange houses and front companies (I-1194); the IRGC claimed three tankers hit mines under US escort, unverified (party claim, I-1193). The level holds at 5 and the trend stays escalating. Reassessed 23 November. Since 17 November: ADNOC Logistics and Services reported that one of its ships was attacked in the strait on the evening of 17 November, with 11 crew injured and one Jordanian crew member missing; the report names no attacker (I-1192). A live-blog entry of 23 November on a further tanker hit and on an Iranian plan to send 14 tankers through the US blockade rests on unconfirmed claims and no permanent article, so neither is added. The level holds at 5 and the trend stays escalating. Reassessed 22 November. Since 21 November: ABC News, citing UKMTO and the IMO, put attacks in and around the strait at 31 in October and about 19 in November as of 18 November, with 34 confirmed by the IMO for October and November so far (I-1184); Bahrain said an Iranian attack hit a civilian industrial facility and started a fire, and the IRGC said it struck US positions at the Al-Riffa and Awali bases (party claims, I-1185). Iran's claim of a US drone shot down over Qeshm rests on state television alone and is not added. The level holds at 5 and the trend stays escalating. Reassessed 21 November. Since 19 November: UKMTO reported a tanker struck by a projectile and set on fire 8 nautical miles north of Khasab on 20 November and, on 21 November, a tanker hit in the stern and a second report of an engine-room hit that may be the same vessel, while the IRGC said the first caught fire on a mine (I-1174); Trump told Axios he is not rushing into any decision on Iran (I-1175). The level holds at 5; the timing of a US strike stays open. Reassessed 20 November. Since 18 November: UKMTO reported a tanker struck by an unknown projectile near the strait off Oman, crew safe (I-1162); Iran's navy claimed two tankers hit mines on 19 November, which Reuters could not verify, and Brent rose to $92.72 (party claim, I-1163). A US strike on Qeshm reported by one outlet could not be dated and is not used. The level holds.
sponsor_posture: Iran (IRGC Navy) is the principal; Tehran frames shipping attacks as leverage over US politics. The US holds the blockade; US officials said US forces struck Iranian targets on Qeshm on 2 November after the Guards fired on a US aircraft, and Washington had earlier pledged no strike on Iran before 3 November.
cyber_nexus: IRGC-linked CyberAv3ngers moved from Unitronics to Rockwell/Allen-Bradley controllers; Iran-linked intrusions hit US water utilities in 12+ states from late July; a UK power plant was shut for four days; about 60 hacktivist groups run DDoS and defacement. No new observed Iran-linked intrusion against US infrastructure was found for 25-27 October.
scenario: An IRGC-aligned persona claims a DDoS and data-leak operation against a US or Gulf payments brand during a spike in tanker attacks, while a separate actor probes internet-exposed OT at a facilities vendor.
so_what: Energy-cost and FX shock, Gulf staff and data-center continuity, and a higher chance of Iranian cyber activity against US financial and payment brands within days of kinetic events.
outlook: Next 72 hours: a US decision on a strike package and Qatari feedback on the two-day sequence are the main variables; further tanker incidents and Iranian claims of mine strikes are likely. Next 30 days (unchanged from the prior review): a strike package stays on the table unless a transit bargain is reached; enforcement against Sinokor tankers would likely cut escorted crude flows.

Next 30 days: no energy truce is reported. A strike disabling a major Russian export terminal for an extended period would argue for CRITICAL.
